tagline: An old town in the valley that's easy to stay in longer than planned
introHtml:
Chiang Mai is the kind of place where you can stroll the old moated city in the morning and drive up the mountain for coffee in the afternoon, all in one day. There are old temples, morning markets, garden cafes, and hills around town to escape the heat and the haze.

Plenty of people come for a few days and head home, but just as many show up and stay for a month, because the pace of life here really is slower than Bangkok in a way you can feel.
bestTime: November–February, cool and clear (skip March–April when the air gets smoky)

highlights.name: The old city moat and Tha Phae Gate
highlights.blurb: The square heart of the old town, lined with dozens of old temples you can spend all day wandering between

highlights.name: Doi Suthep
highlights.blurb: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep sits on a peak overlooking the whole city, the one shrine locals say you should pay respects to at least once

highlights.name: Nimmanhaemin Road
highlights.blurb: The strip of cafes, restaurants, and coworking spaces where the younger crowd and remote workers tend to gather

highlights.name: Sunday Walking Street
highlights.blurb: A night market running the length of Ratchadamnoen Road, with craft stalls, street food, and live music along the way

highlights.name: Mae Rim and San Kamphaeng districts
highlights.blurb: The outskirts packed with cafes in the fields, vegetable gardens, and mountain views, great for an aimless drive

highlights.name: Doi Inthanon
highlights.blurb: Thailand's highest peak, cool all year, with waterfalls and trekking trails through the cloud forest

foodScene.name: Khao soi
foodScene.note: Egg noodles in a coconut-milk curry broth with northern spices, served with chicken or beef, the dish you miss about Chiang Mai before anything else

foodScene.name: Nam ngiao and khanom jeen
foodScene.note: A mildly sour nam ngiao broth over rice noodles, eaten with crispy pork rinds and fresh vegetables, a popular breakfast

foodScene.name: Sai ua and khaep mu
foodScene.note: Northern-style snacks, the herby sausage and crispy pork rinds, sold at morning markets and souvenir shops all over town

foodScene.name: Khantoke and northern food
foodScene.note: A spread of nam phrik ong, nam phrik num, and gaeng hang lay, eaten with sticky rice

foodScene.name: Cafes and hill-grown coffee
foodScene.note: This town has a huge number of coffee shops using beans from the surrounding hills like Mon Cham and Doi Chang

foodScene.name: Morning markets and street food
foodScene.note: Warorot Market (Kad Luang) and Ton Phayom Market are full of fresh produce and ready-made dishes at easy prices

foodScene.name: Mu kratha
foodScene.note: Thai-style grill-and-hotpot spots are everywhere in town, the dinner locals meet up over

attractions.name: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep
attractions.blurb: A hilltop temple reached by climbing the naga staircase to the relic, with views over the whole valley

attractions.name: Wat Chedi Luang
attractions.blurb: A large old chedi in the middle of the old town, a trace of Chiang Mai's Lanna era

attractions.name: Doi Inthanon National Park
attractions.blurb: Thailand's highest peak, with Wachirathan Waterfall, the Kew Mae Pan trail, and the two twin pagodas

attractions.name: Doi Mon Cham
attractions.blurb: A ridgeline farm in Mae Rim district with flower plots and a sea of morning mist

attractions.name: Nimman and Maya
attractions.blurb: The shopping, eating, and hangout district in the newer part of town, with a mall and stylish cafes

attractions.name: Warorot Market (Kad Luang)
attractions.blurb: An old market by the Ping River selling souvenirs, northern snacks, and curry pastes

attractions.name: San Kamphaeng and Bo Sang
attractions.blurb: Home to paper umbrella making and handicrafts, a short drive out of town

attractions.name: San Kamphaeng Hot Springs
attractions.blurb: Natural hot springs where you can soak your feet and boil eggs, a good stop on the way out of town

itineraryIdeas: Chiang Mai 2D1N — old city and Doi Suthep
Chiang Mai cafe run — Nimman and Mae Rim
Chiang Mai for nature — Doi Inthanon and Mon Cham
